skill.displayName: 商机雷达-比招标更早发现机会

llm.summary: This skill mostly does what it says, but it handles account credentials, persistent device identifiers, local report files, and login-bypass links in ways users should review carefully before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses network access and states that registration requires consent, but automatic registration collects and transmits platform, architecture, and a stable SHA-256 MAC hash to an external service, and normal use sends business search terms to the provider API.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No unusual installer or external dependency was found; the package contains markdown instructions and one local Python renderer. Metadata only declares the ZLBX_API_KEY environment requirement and does not enforce the broader file/network behaviors described in prose.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation criteria are broad and the skill directs agents to run API calls and report-rendering commands in the background, generate HTML by default in full mode, expose absolute file paths, and preserve signed URLs without user-controlled redaction.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It persists an API bearer key in ~/.zlbx/config.json and writes shareable HTML reports under ~/zlbx-opportunity-radar-files/; no backdoor or service persistence was found, but credential and report persistence are under-scoped and lack explicit file-permission safeguards.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The procurement-opportunity search purpose is coherent with using Zhiliaobiaoxun APIs, scoring results, and generating reports, but the artifacts require raw sk login-bypass URLs in chat/HTML outputs and add fixed commercial/subscription routing that goes beyond neutral opportunity reporting.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing if you are uncomfortable with a third-party procurement service receiving search terms and a consent-gated MAC-derived device hash. Do not share generated HTML reports or raw links casually, because they may contain login-bypass sk parameters. If installed, prefer setting your own ZLBX_API_KEY, restrict permissions on ~/.zlbx/config.json, and delete exported reports when no longer needed.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad activation language is artifact-backed and can route ambiguous business-development requests into this paid/API-backed workflow; this supports Review but not malicious intent.
[AE1] expected: The referenced render_report.py file was locally present and inspected; this scanner coverage concern is overridden because the artifact was analyzable in this review.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The artifacts explicitly require preserving API-returned URLs with sk login-bypass parameters in chat and HTML, creating a real sharing/logging exposure risk.
[SSD-3] unexpected: The same sk-link requirement applies to exported HTML reports, making signed access links durable and easy to forward.
[SC3] expected: The long base64 value in render_report.py is an inline PNG logo used as an img data URI; no decode-and-execute behavior was found, so this is downgraded.
[LP3] unexpected: Local report writing and credential storage are disclosed in prose but not reflected in enforceable metadata, leaving authority broader than the manifest suggests.
[E1] expected: External transmission during registration is purpose-aligned and consent-gated, but the MAC-derived hash is a persistent device identifier and remains a privacy concern.
[RA2] expected: Saving the API key supports reuse of the service, but storing it as a local JSON bearer credential without required restrictive permissions is a material security concern.
[SQP-2] expected: HTML export is expected for the report feature, but doing it by default and revealing the absolute path can persist and expose sensitive business-lead data without a separate export choice.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-language templates match the apparent product context and are not security-significant by themselves, though users needing another language may have reduced clarity.
[SDI-4] expected: The s86/s88 channel-code inconsistency is a documentation quality issue, not evidence of unsafe behavior by itself.
[T01] unexpected: The static finding is supported in part: mandatory subscription and product links affect report neutrality, but they are visible promotional behavior rather than session hijacking or malware.
[other] expected: The static device-fingerprint finding is supported: the skill hashes MAC addresses only after consent and does not send raw MACs, but the stable identifier still enables device correlation.
[T09] expected: Both static T09 concerns are supported as implementation risks: the API key write lacks mandatory owner-only permissions, and generated HTML accepts unvalidated URL schemes from report data.
